intuition: A path may pass through a node and use both of its child branches. But a path extended to the node's parent can use only one child branch. Calculate both quantities separately: the best complete path through this node, and the best single branch to pass upward.

A child passes up its best single downward branch. Clip a negative branch to zero because omitting it improves any path through its parent. At each node, score a completed path using the node plus both nonnegative child gains.
However, store for the parent only the node plus one larger gain; passing both would create a fork rather than a path.

Children must be processed before their parent. The explicit stack first defers a node with processed=True and pushes its children. When that deferred entry returns, both gains are available. This avoids Python recursion-depth failures on tall trees. Initialize best to negative infinity so an all-negative tree still chooses a real node instead of an empty zero-valued path.

steps: For [-10,9,20,null,null,15,7], process leaf 9 first; its downward gain and completed path both equal 9.
Leaves 15 and 7 likewise contribute gains 15 and 7.
At node 20, the completed path 15→20→7 has sum 42, while its parent-facing gain is 20+15=35.
At root -10, the through-root candidate is -10+9+35=34.
The root can offer gain -10+35=25, but neither root calculation improves best=42.
Return 42, demonstrating why the best possible path need not contain the root.

codeNotes.note: Defer the parent computation until its child gains have been produced.
A completed path may join both branches at its highest node.
A parent extension receives only one branch, preventing an invalid fork.

keyDecision: Use both positive child gains for the complete path, but return only the larger child gain to the parent.

figures.title: A finished path and an upward branch differ
figures.caption: At node 20, the child gains are 15 and 7. The parent is -10. A path may not fork into three branches.

panels.title: Before: both children are solved
panels.note: Each child can offer a positive branch to node 20.

panels.title: Check: score a complete path
panels.note: Using both branches gives 15 → 20 → 7, total 42. This is a complete candidate for the global answer.

panels.title: After: pass only one branch upward
panels.note: Offer 20 + max(15, 7) = 35 to the parent. Passing 42 would let the parent create an invalid fork.
